faq.q: Why is New Year on different dates?
faq.a: Different cultures use different calendars, some based on the Sun, some on the Moon, and some on both. Each calendar starts its year at a different point.
asks: Why are there many New Years?

faq.q: Why does Lunar New Year move?
faq.a: It follows a calendar based on both the Moon and the Sun. It begins with a new moon between 21 January and 20 February, so the date changes each year.

faq.q: When is the Ethiopian New Year?
faq.a: Enkutatash is on 11 September, or 12 September before a leap year. It marks the end of the long rainy season.

faq.q: Why does the Islamic New Year move?
faq.a: The Islamic calendar follows the Moon only. Twelve lunar months make about 354 days, so each new year comes about 11 days earlier than the year before.

faq.q: Which New Years are in April?
faq.a: Around 13 to 14 April many new years are celebrated, including Songkran in Thailand, Aluth Avurudu in Sri Lanka, Pohela Boishakh in Bengal, Vaisakhi in Punjab and Puthandu in Tamil Nadu.

facts: Lunar New Year falls between 21 January and 20 February.
Twelve lunar months last about 354 days, so the Islamic year moves about 11 days earlier each year.
Ethiopia's new year, Enkutatash, is on 11 September (12 September before a Gregorian leap year).
